title: Valuing Compensation a Carrier Settled in Travel Credit
content:
Part of what a carrier pays a traveller for a loss already settled under the Travel Protection Plans may be
given as travel credit rather than money. The carrier's ledger for the traveller's air bookings under the Air Ticket Fare Brands shows both the sum such a credit was issued for and the sum since redeemed against it, and
the travel credit counted toward the compensation is read from those two lines.

## The three readings

| What the carrier's ledger shows | The travel credit counted |
|---|---|
| A credit issued in part settlement of that compensation, standing redeemed in full | The sum the credit was issued for |
| Such a credit standing redeemed in part | The part redeemed |
| Neither of those | Nothing, the traveller having received no money for it |

A credit stands redeemed in full where the sum redeemed against it reaches the sum it was issued for, and
redeemed in part where something has been redeemed but less than that.

## Points of judgement

A credit issued for 600.00 and wholly redeemed counts at 600.00. The same credit with 250.00 redeemed against it
counts at 250.00, the part redeemed and not the sum issued. A credit issued for 600.00 against which nothing at
all has been redeemed counts at nothing, because the traveller has had no money for it; and where the carrier
issued no credit in settlement of that compensation, the travel credit counted is likewise nothing. The amounts
here are hypothetical.
